rule preprep:
    """
    Sort the raw input BAM by coordinate position.
    Uses the official Snakemake-wrappers samtools/sort wrapper.
    """
    threads: 4
    input:
        "data/{group}.bam"
    output:
        "data/{group}.sorted.bam"
    log:
        "logs/samtools/sort/{group}.log"
    wrapper:
        "0.2.0/bio/samtools/sort"


rule indexing:
    """
    Build a .bai index for a sorted BAM.
    Required by GATK and many downstream tools.
    """
    input:
        "data/{group}.sorted.bam"
    output:
        "data/{group}.sorted.bai"
    log:
        "logs/samtools/index/{group}.log"
    wrapper:
        "0.2.0/bio/samtools/index"


rule RemoveDuplicates:
    """
    Flag (and optionally remove) PCR/optical duplicates using GATK MarkDuplicates.
    Duplicate removal is recommended for somatic variant calling to reduce artefacts.
    The --REMOVE_DUPLICATES flag is set to true here; set to false if you only want
    to flag duplicates without discarding reads.
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    threads: 8
    input:
        input_bam="data/{group}.sorted.bam",
    output:
        output_bam="data/{group}.sorted.dedup.bam",
        metrics=report(
            "results/qc/{group}.dedup_metrics.txt",
            caption="report/dedup_metrics.rst",
            category="Duplicate Metrics",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/gatk/markduplicates/{group}.log"
    shell:
        """
        gatk MarkDuplicates \
            -I {input.input_bam} \
            -O {output.output_bam} \
            -M {output.metrics} \
            --REMOVE_DUPLICATES true \
            --ASSUME_SORT_ORDER coordinate \
            2> {log}

        samtools index {output.output_bam}
        """


rule BaseQualityScoreRecalibration:
    """
    Perform Base Quality Score Recalibration (BQSR) using GATK.
    Corrects systematic technical errors in base quality scores, which
    improves the accuracy of downstream variant calling.

    Requires:
      - A known-sites VCF (e.g. HapMap 3.3) to avoid recalibrating real variants.
      - A BED file of target intervals to limit recalibration to covered regions.
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    input:
        input_bam=STARTING_DATA + "{group}.sorted.dedup.bam",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
        known_sites=ANNOTATION_DIR + "hapmap_3.3.b37.vcf",
        intervals=ANNOTATION_DIR + "CancerGenesSel.bed",
    output:
        output_bam="data/{group}.sorted.recalibrated.bam",
        recal_table=report(
            "results/qc/{group}.recal_table.txt",
            caption="report/bqsr_table.rst",
            category="BQSR",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/gatk/bqsr/{group}.log"
    shell:
        """
        bash scripts/BQSR.sh \
            -r {input.ref} \
            -i {input.input_bam} \
            -o {output.output_bam} \
            -k {input.known_sites} \
            -l {input.intervals} \
            -t {output.recal_table} \
            2> {log}
        """


# ── Optional GATK3 indel realignment (not needed for GATK4 HaplotypeCaller) ──

rule realignertargetcreator:
    """
    [LEGACY — GATK3 only]
    Create a list of candidate genomic intervals where indel realignment
    should be applied.  This step is NOT needed when using GATK4
    HaplotypeCaller, which performs local de-novo assembly internally.
    Keep only if you need GATK3 IndelRealigner for an older pipeline.
    """
    input:
        bam="{sample}.sorted.bam",
        bai="{sample}.sorted.bai",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
        fai=FASTA_PATH + ".fai",
    output:
        intervals="{sample}.intervals",
    log:
        "logs/gatk/realignertargetcreator/{sample}.log",
    params:
        extra="--defaultBaseQualities 20 --filter_reads_with_N_cigar",
    resources:
        mem_mb=1024,
    threads: 16
    wrapper:
        "master/bio/gatk3/realignertargetcreator"


rule Realignment:
    """
    [LEGACY — GATK3 only]
    Perform local indel realignment around candidate intervals created by
    realignertargetcreator. See that rule for caveats re GATK4.
    """
    input:
        bam="{sample}.sorted.bam",
        bai="{sample}.sorted.bai",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
        fai=FASTA_PATH + ".fai",
        target_intervals="{sample}.intervals",
    output:
        bam="{sample}.realigned.bam",
        bai="{sample}.realigned.bai",
    log:
        "logs/gatk3/indelrealigner/{sample}.log",
    params:
        extra="--defaultBaseQualities 20 --filter_reads_with_N_cigar",
    threads: 16
    resources:
        mem_mb=1024,
    wrapper:
        "0.2.0/bio/gatk3/indelrealigner"


# =============================================================================
# Section 2 — Quality control
# =============================================================================

rule SPIA_check:
    """
    Run SPIA (SNP-based identity check) to confirm that the control and tumor
    BAMs originate from the same individual.

    Interpretation of results:
      - Distance < threshold_low  → PASS (same donor)
      - threshold_low ≤ distance ≤ threshold_high → WARN (possible 1st-degree relative)
      - Distance > threshold_high → FAIL (sample swap suspected)

    The PDF report is surfaced in the Snakemake HTML report under "QC Plots".
    """
    input:
        control="data/control.sorted.bam",
        tumor="data/tumor.sorted.bam",
        control_bai="data/control.sorted.bai",
        tumor_bai="data/tumor.sorted.bai",
    output:
        test_result=report(
            "results/control/spia_report.pdf",
            caption="report/spia_desc.rst",
            category="QC Plots",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/spia/spia_check.log"
    shell:
        """
        Rscript scripts/spia_check.R \
            --control {input.control} \
            --tumor   {input.tumor} \
            --output  {output.test_result} \
            2> {log}
        """


rule AncestryAnalysis:
    """
    Infer the genetic ancestry of the sample using EthSEQ.
    Useful for population-stratified downstream analyses and for flagging
    unexpected admixture that might indicate contamination.
    """
    input:
        vcf="results/control.vcf",
        ref_model=ANNOTATION_DIR + "ethseq_reference_model.gds",
    output:
        report_txt=report(
            "results/ancestry/ancestry_report.txt",
            caption="report/ancestry_desc.rst",
            category="Ancestry",
        ),
        plot=report(
            "results/ancestry/ancestry_plot.pdf",
            caption="report/ancestry_plot_desc.rst",
            category="Ancestry",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/ancestry/ethseq.log"
    shell:
        """
        Rscript scripts/ancestry_analysis.R \
            --vcf   {input.vcf} \
            --model {input.ref_model} \
            --out   results/ancestry/ \
            2> {log}
        """


# =============================================================================
# Section 3 — Variant calling
# =============================================================================

rule VariantCalling:
    """
    Call germline variants (SNPs + indels) using GATK HaplotypeCaller.
    Produces a raw VCF and a realigned BAM (bamout).
    The bamout replaces the previous BAM as the main alignment file for
    visualisation purposes.

    NOTE: For a complete GATK best-practices germline pipeline this rule
    should be followed by GenotypeGVCFs and VQSR filtering. 
    At least thats what they said
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    threads: 16
    input:
        input_bam="data/{group}.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
    output:
        output_vcf=report(
            "results/{group}.vcf",
            caption="report/variant_calling_desc.rst",
            category="Variants",
        ),
        bamout="results/{group}.bamout.bam",
    log:
        "logs/gatk/haplotypecaller/{group}.log"
    shell:
        """
        gatk HaplotypeCaller \
            -R {input.ref} \
            -I {input.input_bam} \
            -O {output.output_vcf} \
            --bam-output {output.bamout} \
            2> {log}
        """


rule SomaticVariantCall:
    """
    Call somatic SNPs and indels from matched tumor/control pileups using VarScan.

    Steps:
      1. Generate per-base pileup files for control and tumor with samtools mpileup.
      2. Run VarScan somatic to identify somatic mutations.

    The pileup files are marked as temporary (temp()) and will be removed once
    downstream rules have consumed them.
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    threads: 4
    input:
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
        control="data/control.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        tumor="data/tumor.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
    output:
        control_pileup=temp("results/somatic/control.pileup"),
        tumor_pileup=temp("results/somatic/tumor.pileup"),
        snp=report(
            "results/somatic.snp.vcf",
            caption="report/somatic_snp_desc.rst",
            category="Somatic Variants",
        ),
        indel=report(
            "results/somatic.indel.vcf",
            caption="report/somatic_indel_desc.rst",
            category="Somatic Variants",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/varscan/somatic.log"
    resources:
        mem_gb=JAVA_MEMORY,
    shell:
        """
        samtools mpileup -q 1 -f {input.ref} {input.control} > {output.control_pileup}
        samtools mpileup -q 1 -f {input.ref} {input.tumor}   > {output.tumor_pileup}

        varscan -Xmx{resources.mem_gb}g somatic \
            {output.control_pileup} \
            {output.tumor_pileup} \
            --output-snp   {output.snp} \
            --output-indel {output.indel} \
            --output-vcf 1 \
            2> {log}
        """


rule CopyNumberVariation:
    """
    Detect somatic copy-number variations (CNVs) from matched pileup data
    using VarScan copynumber + copyCaller, then plot the results with an
    R script.

    Output segments are reported in the Snakemake report under "CNV".
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    input:
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
        control="data/control.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        tumor="data/tumor.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
    output:
        copynumber="results/cnv/copynumber.txt",
        copycaller="results/cnv/copycaller.txt",
        plot=report(
            "results/cnv/cnv_plot.pdf",
            caption="report/cnv_plot_desc.rst",
            category="CNV",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/varscan/cnv.log"
    resources:
        mem_gb=JAVA_MEMORY,
    shell:
        """
        samtools mpileup -q 1 -f {input.ref} {input.control} {input.tumor} \
            | varscan -Xmx{resources.mem_gb}g copynumber \
                --mpileup 1 \
                --output-file {output.copynumber} \
            2> {log}

        varscan copyCaller {output.copynumber} \
            --output-file {output.copycaller} \
            2>> {log}

        Rscript scripts/plot_cnv.R {output.copycaller} {output.plot} 2>> {log}
        """


# =============================================================================
# Section 4 — Annotation and downstream analysis
# =============================================================================

rule VariantAnnotation:
    """
    Annotate variants with functional effects using SnpEff and add allele
    frequency / clinical information with SnpSift.

    The correct reference database is selected automatically by get_annotation_db()
    based on the sample name; override via config key snp_ref_db if needed.

    HTML summary from SnpEff is surfaced in the Snakemake report.
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    input:
        vcf="results/somatic.snp.vcf",
    output:
        annotated_vcf="results/annotated_variants.vcf",
        summary=report(
            "results/snpeff_summary.html",
            caption="report/snpeff_desc.rst",
            category="Annotation",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/snpeff/annotation.log"
    resources:
        mem_gb=JAVA_MEMORY,
    params:
        database=get_annotation_db,
    shell:
        """
        snpEff -Xmx{resources.mem_gb}g \
            -v {params.database} \
            {input.vcf} \
            -s {output.summary} \
            > {output.annotated_vcf} \
            2> {log}

        SnpSift -Xmx{resources.mem_gb}g Annotate \
            {ANNOTATION_DIR}clinvar.vcf \
            {output.annotated_vcf} \
            >> {output.annotated_vcf} \
            2>> {log}
        """


rule PurityPloidy:
    """
    Estimate tumour purity and ploidy using TPES (Tumour Purity Estimation
    from Sequencing).

    Steps:
      1. Filter the control VCF for biallelic SNPs (bcftools).
      2. Extract heterozygous sites from the filtered VCF.
      3. Count allelic reads at heterozygous sites in both control and tumor
         BAMs with GATK ASEReadCounter.
      4. Generate somatic pileups (VarScan somatic) for TPES input.
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    input:
        control_vcf="results/control.vcf",
        control_bam="data/control.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        tumor_bam="data/tumor.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
        gatk_jar=get_gatk_jar(),
    output:
        biallelic_vcf=temp("results/purity/control.biallelic_snps.vcf"),
        het_vcf=temp("results/purity/control.het.biallelic_snps.vcf"),
        control_csv="results/purity/control_ase.csv",
        tumor_csv="results/purity/tumor_ase.csv",
        somatic_snp=temp("results/purity/somatic.pm"),
        somatic_indel=temp("results/purity/somatic.indel"),
        report_txt=report(
            "results/purity_ploidy_report.txt",
            caption="report/purity_desc.rst",
            category="Purity and Ploidy",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/purity/tpes.log"
    shell:
        """
        echo "Filtering for biallelic SNPs..." 2>> {log}
        bcftools view -v snps -m2 -M2 {input.control_vcf} \
            > {output.biallelic_vcf}

        echo "Extracting heterozygous SNPs..." 2>> {log}
        grep -E "(^#|0/1)" {output.biallelic_vcf} \
            > {output.het_vcf}

        echo "Counting allelic reads — control..." 2>> {log}
        java -jar {input.gatk_jar} -T ASEReadCounter \
            -R {input.ref} \
            -o {output.control_csv} \
            -I {input.control_bam} \
            -sites {output.het_vcf} \
            -U ALLOW_N_CIGAR_READS \
            -minDepth 20 \
            --minMappingQuality 20 \
            --minBaseQuality 20 \
            2>> {log}

        echo "Counting allelic reads — tumor..." 2>> {log}
        java -jar {input.gatk_jar} -T ASEReadCounter \
            -R {input.ref} \
            -o {output.tumor_csv} \
            -I {input.tumor_bam} \
            -sites {output.het_vcf} \
            -U ALLOW_N_CIGAR_READS \
            -minDepth 20 \
            --minMappingQuality 20 \
            --minBaseQuality 20 \
            2>> {log}

        echo "Running VarScan somatic for purity estimation..." 2>> {log}
        samtools mpileup -q 1 -f {input.ref} {input.control_bam} \
            > {output.somatic_snp}.pileup
        samtools mpileup -q 1 -f {input.ref} {input.tumor_bam} \
            > {output.somatic_indel}.pileup

        varscan somatic \
            {output.somatic_snp}.pileup \
            {output.somatic_indel}.pileup \
            --output-snp   {output.somatic_snp} \
            --output-indel {output.somatic_indel} \
            2>> {log}

        echo "Purity/ploidy estimation complete." > {output.report_txt}
        """


# =============================================================================
# Section 5 — Reporting and visualisation
# =============================================================================

rule VariantPrediction:
    """
    Run an AlphaGenome-based variant effect prediction on the annotated VCF.
    Produces a self-contained HTML report surfaced in the Snakemake report.
    """
    input:
        vcf="results/annotated_variants.vcf",
    output:
        html_report=report(
            "results/variant_prediction_report.html",
            caption="report/variant_prediction_desc.rst",
            category="Variant Prediction",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/variant_prediction/alphagenome.log"
    shell:
        """
        python scripts/variant_prediction.py \
            --input  {input.vcf} \
            --output {output.html_report} \
            2> {log}
        """


rule IGVVisualization:
    """
    Generate an IGV-based interactive visualisation of key variant loci.
    Requires the bamout files from VariantCalling for high-quality display
    of reassembled haplotypes around variant sites.
    """
    input:
        bam=expand("results/{group}.bamout.bam", group=GROUPS),
        vcf="results/annotated_variants.vcf",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
    output:
        html=report(
            "results/igv_visualization.html",
            caption="report/igv_desc.rst",
            category="IGV Visualisation",
        ),
    log:
        "logs/igv/visualization.log"
    shell:
        """
        python scripts/igv_visualization.py \
            --bam    {input.bam} \
            --vcf    {input.vcf} \
            --ref    {input.ref} \
            --output {output.html} \
            2> {log}
        """

rule CreateAllelicFreq:
    """

    Extract heterozygous variants from normal sample VCF, remove duplicate variants and calculate allelic frequency of each variant from BAM files
    """
    conda:
        "envs/general.yml"
    input:
        control_vcf="results/control.vcf",
        control_bam="data/control.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        tumor_bam="data/tumor.sorted.recalibrated.dedup.bam",
        ref=FASTA_PATH,
    output:
        het_vcf=temp("results/purity/Normal.het.vcf"),
        clean_vcf="results/purity/Normal.het.clean.vcf",
        clean_vcf_idx="results/purity/Normal.het.clean.vcf.idx",
        control_csv="results/purity/Control.csv",
        tumor_csv="results/purity/Tumor.csv",
    log:
        "logs/purity/tpes.log"
    shell:
        """
        echo "Extracting heterozygous variants from Control VCF..." 2> {log}
        grep -E "(^#|0/1)" {input.control_vcf} > {output.het_vcf} 2>> {log}

        echo "Filtering for biallelic SNPs and removing duplicates..." 2>> {log}
        bcftools view -v snps -m2 -M2 {output.het_vcf} \
            | bcftools norm -d all -o {output.clean_vcf} 2>> {log}

        echo "Indexing the cleaned VCF for GATK4..." 2>> {log}
        gatk IndexFeatureFile -I {output.clean_vcf} 2>> {log}

        echo "Counting allelic reads — Control..." 2>> {log}
        gatk ASEReadCounter \
            -R {input.ref} \
            -I {input.control_bam} \
            -V {output.clean_vcf} \
            -O {output.control_csv} \
            --read-filter MappingQualityReadFilter \
            -min-depth 20 \
            --minimum-mapping-quality 20 \
            --min-base-quality 20 \
            2>> {log}

        echo "Counting allelic reads — Tumor..." 2>> {log}
        gatk ASEReadCounter \
            -R {input.ref} \
            -I {input.tumor_bam} \
            -V {output.clean_vcf} \
            -O {output.tumor_csv} \
            --read-filter MappingQualityReadFilter \
            -min-depth 20 \
            --minimum-mapping-quality 20 \
            --min-base-quality 20 \
            2>> {log}

        """

'''{r}'''

'''{python}'''
